text:
maria: quick sanity check — i'm about to land a terraform change for the vectorizer service that wires IRSA -> KMS decrypt. planning order: create kms key + alias, create iam role + role policy, create iam role binding (annotation on k8s SA), then helm release for vectorizer. any obvious races here?

jack: that ordering sounds right in intent but watch out if helm creates the ServiceAccount itself. if helm creates the SA, the annotation from terraform (kubernetes_manifest or kubernetes_service_account) might race. two options:
- let helm create the SA and patch annotation via a short k8s job after helm
- or set `serviceAccount.create=false` in the chart values and manage the SA in k8s provider (so tf controls annotation).

sam: ^^ + also ensure the IAM role exists before you try to annotate with `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn`. i've seen plans succeed locally but apply reorder in CI if resources are independent. add explicit depends_on from the k8s SA resource to the aws_iam_role if you manage the SA in terraform.

maria: noted. i actually have the SA managed in the chart by default. i'd rather avoid editing chart. can we do a small k8s Job that patches the SA annotation after helm? something like:
```bash
kubectl annotate sa vectorizer -n ingest eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn=arn:aws:iam::111111:role/vectorizer-irsa --overwrite
```
would that be fine?

tina: that's ok as a pragmatic fix. CI pattern we've used before: helm deploy -> wait for helm hook -> `kubectl annotate` job as a post-deploy step, then wait-for-rollout. also consider adding a small retry loop in the job because the SA sometimes takes a couple seconds to exist.

jack: about KMS grants: make the grant resource refer to the role ARN (grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.vectorizer.arn) not the assumed-role principal. and create the key with key_usage and rotation as required. example snippet we've used: 
```hcl
resource "aws_kms_key" "vector_key" { ... }
resource "aws_iam_role" "vectorizer" { ... assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.irsa.json }
resource "aws_kms_grant" "vector_grant" {
  name               = "vectorizer-grant"
  key_id             = aws_kms_key.vector_key.key_id
  grantee_principal  = aws_iam_role.vectorizer.arn
  operations         = ["Decrypt"]
}
```
mention: grant is eventual; you may need to re-run apply if the role ARN isn't resolvable yet.

maria: good point. in our modules the role is created in `modules/infra/iam` and the helm release in `modules/k8s/vectorizer`. currently there's no cross-module depends_on linking. i'll add an output role_arn from iam module and feed it into k8s module then create a null_resource in the k8s module that depends_on([module.iam.role_arn, aws_kms_key.vector_key]) and runs the annotate shell.

sam: small nit — prefer using `local-exec` on a `null_resource` only as last resort. alternatively, add a terraform `kubernetes_manifest` resource for the SA that sets the annotation (this keeps everything in tf graph and avoids external shell steps). but i know chart ownership can make that awkward.

maria: ok i'll do this: 1) create role + key + grant 2) expose role_arn output 3) set chart value `serviceAccount.annotations.eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` via `helm_release` values interpolation (so helm applies annotation directly) or fallback to null_resource patch job if chart can't accept that value. i'll try helm first.

jack: one more: make sure the OIDC provider exists in the account (data.aws_iam_openid_connect_provider) and that the role assume_policy references the provider ARN. if your infra code splits provider creation, add a dependency.

deploy-bot: plan started for branch feature/vectorizer-irsa (CI): https://ci.example.com/build/987

maria: thanks all — i'll push a draft PR with tf snippets and a CI job for post-helm annotate if needed, and ping once i have the plan green.

tina: thx — if you want me to watch the first deploy, ping here and i'll stand by. :thumbsup:
